data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 claims the panel produces more reliable judgments via 'stochastic error cancellation' coordinated by the checklist, but the checklist mechanism described — 'ensures all panel members look at the same features' — introduces correlated errors rather than independent ones. If all members are directed to inspect identical features in identical fashion, individual errors are not independent draws; they are structurally coupled by the shared procedure. The Law of Large Numbers requires independent (or at least sufficiently uncorrelated) error terms to cancel, but the very coordination mechanism SRC_003 identifies as the checklist's function undermines the independence assumption its reliability claim depends on. The decoy-item test for compliance-vs-reliability is well-constructed, but the core explanatory mechanism is self-contradictory.
